entries.text_de:
Cambridge Corpus Christi College 70, geschrieben um 1310—15. Einst besessen und corrigirt vom Londoner Stadtkämmerer Andreas Horn14 († 1328), um 131015, enthält die Leges Angl. Londoniis s. XIII. in. coll.16; s. u. Lond. Darin aus Quadr. p. 4 Ine, u. S. 89; p. 9 Blas; Forf, u. S. 389; p. 9 Hu, u. S. 192; p. 10 Af von El. 49, 9 an, u. S. 47; p. 16 AGu, u. S. 127; p. 17 App AGu, u. S. 394; EGu, u. S. 129; p. 19 I As; As Alm; II As, u. S. 147. 151; p. 23 Episc, u. S. 477; Norðleod; Mirce, u. S. 459 f.; p. 24 Að; Had, u. S. 465; p. 25 IV. V. III. VI As, u. S. 171. 167. 170. 173; p. 30 Ordal, u. S. 386; p. 31—36 Iud Dei XVI. I. XV, u. S. 427. 401. 427; p. 37 Cnut, u. S. 279 [auf den Rändern von p. 40—53 ist um 1320 sicut apud S. Augustinum Cantuar., d. h. aus T, manches Quadrip.-Stück nachgetragen und von Or theilweise in den Text aufgenommen: II Eg 4. 3; Swer; Pax; IV Atr 3; III Eg 8; Quadr. Arg. 1. 9—11, u. S. 199. 197. 397. 391. 234. 205. 532 f.] — P. 53 Wl art Lond retr, u. S. 489; p. 55 ECf retr Lond interp., u. S. 627; p. 75 Hn, u. S. 547 (mit p. 76 f. CHn cor und Hn Lond, u. S. 521. 524). Auf p. 188 steht theilweise Lib Lond, u. S. 673.

Co ward theilweise copirt in Or Ed.
entries.text_en:
Cambridge Corpus Christi College 70, written c. 1310—15. Once owned and corrected by the London city chamberlain Andrew Horn14 († 1328), c. 131015; contains the Leges Angl. Londoniis s. XIII. in. coll.16; see below, Lond. In it, from Quadr.: p. 4 Ine, below, p. 89; p. 9 Blas; Forf, below, p. 389; p. 9 Hu, below, p. 192; p. 10 Af from El. 49, 9 onwards, below, p. 47; p. 16 AGu, below, p. 127; p. 17 App AGu, below, p. 394; EGu, below, p. 129; p. 19 I As; As Alm; II As, below, pp. 147. 151; p. 23 Episc, below, p. 477; Norðleod; Mirce, below, p. 459 f.; p. 24 Að; Had, below, p. 465; p. 25 IV. V. III. VI As, below, pp. 171. 167. 170. 173; p. 30 Ordal, below, p. 386; pp. 31—36 Iud Dei XVI. I. XV, below, pp. 427. 401. 427; p. 37 Cnut, below, p. 279 [in the margins of pp. 40—53, c. 1320, sicut apud S. Augustinum Cantuar., i.e. from T, many a Quadrip. passage has been added, and partly taken into the text by Or: II Eg 4. 3; Swer; Pax; IV Atr 3; III Eg 8; Quadr. Arg. 1. 9—11, below, pp. 199. 197. 397. 391. 234. 205. 532 f.] — P. 53 Wl art Lond retr, below, p. 489; p. 55 ECf retr Lond interp., below, p. 627; p. 75 Hn, below, p. 547 (with pp. 76 f. CHn cor and Hn Lond, below, pp. 521. 524). On p. 188 stands, in part, Lib Lond, below, p. 673.

Co was partly copied in Or Ed.

notes.text_de: Er nennt sich p. 101; in Initialen erscheint oft ein Fisch: Horn war Fischhändler. Vgl. u. Horn.
notes.text_en: He names himself on p. 101; a fish often appears in the initials: Horn was a fishmonger. Cf. below, Horn.

notes.text_de: p. 17: ista lex tenetur tempore Edwardi [I] auch in K, also der Vorlage entnommen; dagegen p. 190 temporibus Edwardi fil. Edw.
notes.text_en: p. 17: ista lex tenetur tempore Edwardi [I] also in K, hence taken from the exemplar; whereas p. 190 has temporibus Edwardi fil. Edw.

notes.text_de: Leges Angl. S. 2; Maitland zum Mirrour of justices ed. Whitaker p. xvi. [Vgl. hierüber Dt. Literaturztg. 1895, 1100.] Horn sprach Französisch laut Co p. 41.
notes.text_en: Leges Angl. p. 2; Maitland on the Mirrour of justices, ed. Whitaker, p. xvi. [Cf. on this Dt. Literaturztg. 1895, 1100.] Horn spoke French, according to Co p. 41.

transcription.doubts: Small capitals 'xvi' in n. 16 given in lower case.

A copy of the London collection made in the first half of the fourteenth century, now split between two Corpus Christi College, Cambridge manuscripts, and given to the Guildhall. Wormald identifies it as Andrew Horn's working copy, as distinct from his larger presentation copies, K2 and Or.
